note: Land to government. The key is the Census's own AIANNH code, which a reservation and its off-reservation trust land share. Governments are named exactly as the Bureau of Indian Affairs names them in data/bia-tribal-governments.json. Kentucky is covered with NO AREAS, which is a measurement rather than an omission: all six AIANNH layers return zero features over the state's whole extent, with North Carolina run as a control on the same six queries and answering 7, 2 and 2 on three of them, so the queries work. Re-measured 2026-09-30 at that instance's go-live. Arkansas is covered with no areas too, measured 2026-10-15 at its go-live: the three drawn classes return 499 features nationally and none is kept inside Arkansas, with Tennessee run as a control on the same queries and keeping its one known piece, the Mississippi Choctaw trust land near Henning (0.695 km2). The Cherokee and Choctaw statistical areas that reach over Arkansas's western line are statistical areas, which are drawn only in Oklahoma. OKLAHOMA IS THE ONE STATE WHERE STATISTICAL AREAS ARE ENTERED (Adam, 2026-10-10, "Make an exception for OK"): its Oklahoma Tribal Statistical Areas and joint-use areas carry land classes `otsa` and `joint-use`, and tribal_areas.DRAWN_STATISTICAL is what allows them. Where the Census's own name for one area names several nations, the entry lists each under `governments`, matched to the Bureau's list by that name; nations seated inside an area whose name does not name them (the United Keetoowah Band, the Delaware Tribe of Indians and the Alabama-Quassarte, Kialegee and Thlopthlocco tribal towns) are not entered here; scripts/build_tribal_areas.py places them by their seat city and the card lists them as seated in that area. The Shawnee Trust Land is matched to the Shawnee Tribe by the Census's basename. Mississippi is covered from 2026-10-15, measured while its instance was still dark: the Census keeps two pieces there, both the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians' (code 2300), the Mississippi Choctaw Reservation (123.468 km2, all of it in the state) and its off-reservation trust land (16.396 km2 of 17.092, 95.9%). The trust land's other 0.695 km2 is Tennessee's piece, entered with Tennessee. Louisiana is covered from 2026-10-20, measured while its instance was still dark: the Census keeps six pieces there, four reservations and two off-reservation trust lands, held by four governments, every piece wholly inside the state: the Chitimacha Tribe of Louisiana (code 0635, its reservation, 1.819 km2), the Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana (0795, its reservation, 2.761 km2, and its trust land, 8.592 km2), the Jena Band of Choctaw Indians (1690, its reservation, 1.763 km2) and the Tunica-Biloxi Indian Tribe (4315, its reservation, 1.690 km2, and its trust land, 4.412 km2). Missouri is covered with no areas, measured 2026-10-26 at its go-live (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Missouri): the three drawn classes keep no feature inside the state, with Missouri resolving to state code 29 as the control. Virginia is covered from 2026-10-30, measured while its instance was still dark (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Virginia): the Census keeps three pieces there, every one wholly inside the state. Two are State American Indian Reservations, the Pamunkey (state) Reservation (code 9260, 6.380 km2), held by the Pamunkey Indian Tribe, which the United States has recognized since 2016 and the Bureau lists, and the Mattaponi (state) Reservation (9230, 0.311 km2), held by the Mattaponi Tribe, which Virginia recognizes and the United States does not. The third is the Rappahannock Trust Land (3075, 0.556 km2), held by the Rappahannock Tribe. The Chickahominy and Eastern Chickahominy statistical areas are statistical areas, drawn only in Oklahoma, and the Monacan, Nansemond and Upper Mattaponi hold no land the Census draws. West Virginia is covered with no areas, measured 2026-11-10 at its go-live (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report "West Virginia"): the three drawn classes keep no feature inside the state, with West Virginia resolving to state code 54 as the control. Georgia was recorded as not yet covered at its go-live on 2026-11-10, when its app drew no tribal land, and is covered from 2026-11-13 (below). The Georgia Tribe of Eastern Cherokee's area is a state designated tribal statistical area, which is drawn only in Oklahoma. Pennsylvania, New Jersey and New Hampshire are covered with no areas, measured 2026-11-11 at their go-live (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report <state>): the three drawn classes keep no feature inside any of the three, with each state resolving to its own state code (42, 34, 33) as the control. Arizona and Nevada were recorded as not yet covered the same day (az/WATCH.md, nv/WATCH.md); both are covered from 2026-11-12. Ohio is covered with no areas, measured 2026-11-11 at its go-live (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Ohio): the three drawn classes keep no feature inside the state, with Ohio resolving to state code 39 as the control. Washington was recorded as not yet covered the same day, with Texas and Florida; all three are covered from 2026-11-12. Delaware, Hawaii and Vermont are covered with no areas, measured 2026-11-12 at their go-live (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report <state>): the three drawn classes keep no feature inside any of the three, with each state resolving to its own state code (10, 15, 50) as the control. New Mexico, Nebraska, Idaho, Maine, Montana, Rhode Island, South Dakota, North Dakota, Alaska and Wyoming are NOT YET covered, recorded the same day: none of those ten apps draws tribal land yet (each one's WATCH.md). Texas is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Texas, with Texas resolving to state code 48 as the control): the Census keeps six pieces there, held by three governments, every piece wholly inside the state: the Alabama-Coushatta Tribe of Texas (code 0050, its reservation, 18.521 km2, and its trust land, 18.307 km2), the Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas (1775, its reservation, 1.557 km2, and its trust land, 0.133 km2) and Ysleta del Sur Pueblo (4755, its reservation, 0.299 km2, and its trust land, 12.760 km2). Florida is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Florida, state code 12 as the control): the Census keeps eleven pieces there. The Miccosukee Tribe of Indians holds the Miccosukee Reservation (2240, 310.165 km2) and its trust land (20.341 km2). The Seminole Tribe of Florida holds six reservations, each under its own code, which the tribe's own site lists as its reservations (www.semtribe.com, read 2026-11-12): Big Cypress (0225, 213.677 km2), Brighton (0360, 148.241 km2), Fort Pierce (1260, 0.245 km2), Hollywood (1475, 2.049 km2), Immokalee (1555, 2.492 km2) and Tampa (4130, 0.182 km2). It also holds the Seminole (FL) Trust Land (3665, 0.004 km2), which the Census names for it, and the Coconut Creek Trust Land (0690, 0.026 km2), whose Census name names no nation: the tribe's own gaming page lists its Seminole Casino Coconut Creek, and the parcel's interior point (26.2776, -80.1999) lies in the city of Coconut Creek, so it is entered as the Seminole Tribe's. The eleventh piece is a 0.007 km2 part of the Poarch Creek Off-Reservation Trust Land (2865, 1.37% of that parcel), whose government is in Alabama; it is entered with Florida only, since Alabama is not yet covered. Washington is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Washington, with Washington resolving to state code 53 as the control): the Census keeps 50 pieces there, 28 reservations and 22 pieces of off-reservation trust land, under 29 codes, each code held by one government and every piece but one wholly inside the state. The Port Madison Reservation (2925) is entered as the Suquamish Indian Tribe's, which the Bureau names as the Suquamish Indian Tribe of the Port Madison Reservation. The exception is the Umatilla Off-Reservation Trust Land (4405), of which 43.353 km2, 71.4%, lies in Washington; its government, the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation, is seated in Pendleton, Oregon, and it is entered with Washington only, since Oregon is not yet covered. The Samish Indian Nation, which the Bureau seats in Anacortes, holds no land the Census draws in Washington and has no entry. Arizona is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Arizona, with Arizona resolving to state code 04 as the control): the Census keeps 28 pieces there, 21 reservations and 7 pieces of off-reservation trust land, under 21 codes, each code held by one government. Five of the reservations cross the state line, and each is entered with Arizona only, since none of California, Nevada, New Mexico or Utah is yet covered: the Navajo Nation Reservation (2430), of which 41,853.030 km2, 71.6%, lies in Arizona, and of whose trust land 28.779 km2, 0.6%; the Colorado River Indian Reservation (0735), 83.8%; the Fort Mojave Reservation (1235), 70.0%, whose government the Bureau seats in Needles, California; the Fort Yuma Indian Reservation (1280), 4.6%, the Quechan Tribe's, seated in Winterhaven, California; and the Zuni Reservation (4785), 3.1%, the Zuni Tribe's, seated in Zuni, New Mexico. The Census's Maricopa (Ak Chin) Indian Reservation (2130) is entered as the Ak-Chin Indian Community's, its Yavapai-Apache Nation Reservation (4708) as the Yavapai-Apache Nation of the Camp Verde Indian Reservation's, and its Pascua Pueblo Yaqui Reservation (2680) as the Pascua Yaqui Tribe's. The San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe of Arizona, recognized and listed by the Bureau with no state and no city, holds no land the Census draws and has no entry. Nevada is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report Nevada, with Nevada resolving to state code 32 as the control): the Census keeps 35 pieces there, 27 reservations and 8 pieces of off-reservation trust land, under 28 codes held by 20 governments. The Te-Moak Tribe of Western Shoshone holds four codes, its constituent bands' colonies at Battle Mountain (0165), Elko (1005), South Fork (3930) and Wells (4580), which the Bureau lists as one government; the Washoe Tribe four, Carson Colony (0510), Dresslerville Colony (0940), Stewart Community (3980) and Washoe Ranches Trust Land (4560); the Yerington Paiute Tribe two, Campbell Ranch (0440) and Yerington Colony (4725); and the Fallon Paiute-Shoshone Tribe two, its colony (1070) and its reservation (1075). Six cross the state line and are entered with Nevada only, since none of California, Idaho, Oregon or Utah is yet covered: the Duck Valley Reservation (0965), 49.7% in Nevada; the Fort McDermitt Indian Reservation (1210), 48.0%; the Goshute Reservation (1340), 58.4%; the Timbi-Sha Shoshone Reservation (4180), 78.1%, whose government the Bureau seats in Bishop, California; the Washoe Ranches Trust Land (4560), 99.7%; and the Fort Mojave Reservation (1235), 11.5%, already entered for Arizona and given its Nevada piece. EIGHT OF THESE GOVERNMENTS THE BUREAU LISTS WITH NO OFFICE TOWN, neither a city nor a state, and Adam chose on 2026-11-12 to take the town from each nation's own site, keeping to robots.txt and never working around a challenge, and where a nation has no such site to draw its land and say the Bureau lists no office town. Seven are entered with `seatFromNation`, giving the town, the page it was read on, the date and why; for the Duck Valley and Goshute nations the Bureau's site address no longer reaches the nation's own page, and `bureauWebsiteWithdrawn` says what it served instead. Nevada's Department of Native American Affairs gives the same town for all seven. The Winnemucca Indian Colony (4635) has no site of its own that was found, and is entered with `seatFromState`: the town, Reno, of the address Nevada's Department of Native American Affairs lists for its chair, which Adam said yes to the same day. Only the town is carried. California is covered from 2026-11-12 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report California, with California resolving to state code 06 as the control): the Census keeps 150 pieces there, 103 reservations and rancherias and 47 pieces of off-reservation trust land, under 106 codes held by 98 governments. The Pit River Tribe holds seven codes, the Big Bend (0215), Likely (1955), Lookout (1980), Montgomery Creek (2330), Roaring Creek (3185) and XL Ranch (4680) rancherias and the Pit River Trust Land (2835): the Census's names for the six rancherias do not name the tribe, and the tribe's own history page (pitrivertribe.gov/tribal-history/, read 2026-11-12) names its land as including the XL Ranch, Montgomery Creek, Roaring Creek, Big Bend, Burney, Lookout and Likely rancherias. The Capitan Grande Reservation (0495) is entered under `governments` with the two groups the Bureau lists under the Capitan Grande Band, the Barona Group and the Viejas (Baron Long) Group: the Census's name names the band, the Bureau lists the band itself with neither a city, a state nor a site and lists the two groups each with a seat, and Barona's own history page (barona-nsn.gov/history, read 2026-11-12) says the federal government established the reservation in 1875 and a group of its members later bought the Barona Ranch. Each group also holds its own reservation, Barona (0155) and Viejas (4500). The Bureau seats two of these governments outside the state: the Colorado River Indian Tribes in Parker, Arizona, and the Washoe Tribe in Gardnerville, Nevada, whose Woodfords Community (4665) lies wholly in California. Five codes entered before for Arizona or Nevada are given their California pieces: the Colorado River Indian Reservation (0735), 16.2% in California; the Fort Mojave Reservation (1235), 18.5%, and its off-reservation trust land, which lies wholly in California; the Fort Yuma Indian Reservation (1280), 95.4%; the Timbi-Sha Shoshone Reservation (4180), 21.9%, and its off-reservation trust land, also wholly in California; and the Washoe Ranches Trust Land (4560), 0.3%. The Bureau lists two of these governments with no office town, neither a city nor a state, and under Adam's choice of 2026-11-12 for Nevada each is entered with `seatFromNation`, the town its own site gives: the Round Valley Indian Tribes (3250) at Covelo and the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation (3265), on the Census's Rumsey Indian Rancheria, at Brooks. The Bureau also lists the Koi Nation of Northern California and the California Valley Miwok Tribe with no office town; neither holds land the Census draws, so neither is entered. The Greenville Rancheria's government the Bureau lists with a state and no city, so its card gives the state alone. Alabama, Colorado, Connecticut, Georgia, Kansas, Oregon and Utah are covered from 2026-11-13 (scripts/tribal_areas.py --report <state>, each state resolving to its own state code as the control); Massachusetts is NOT YET covered (ma/WATCH.md): the Census keeps three pieces there, the Mashpee Wampanoag and Wampanoag-Aquinnah trust lands and the Hassanamisco (state) Reservation, and no page of the Commonwealth's that states the Hassanamisco Nipmuc's recognition could be read, because www.mass.gov refuses this project. Alabama: three pieces. The Poarch Band of Creek Indians' reservation (2865, 1.079 km2) and 98.6%% of its off-reservation trust land, whose Florida piece was entered with Florida; and the MOWA Choctaw (state) Reservation (9240, 2.694 km2), held by the MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians, which the State of Alabama recognizes and the United States does not, named from the Alabama Indian Affairs Commission's list of tribes the state recognizes. Colorado: two pieces, the Southern Ute Reservation (3925, 2,759.162 km2) and 80.5%% of the Ute Mountain Reservation (4470), whose Utah piece and trust land are entered with Utah. Connecticut: six pieces. The Mashantucket Pequot Indian Tribe holds its reservation and trust land (2145) and the Mohegan Tribe its reservation (2320); the three State American Indian Reservations are held by tribes the State of Connecticut recognizes and the United States does not, named as the tribal affairs page of the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection names them: the Golden Hill Paugussett (9100), the Eastern Pequot Tribal Nation (9280, on the Census's Paucatuck Eastern Pequot (state) Reservation) and the Schaghticoke Tribe (9350), which that page says has two factions. Georgia: one piece, the Tama (state) Reservation (9400, 0.367 km2), held by the Lower Muscogee Creek Tribe, which Code Section 44-12-300, as House Bill 43 of 2024 amended it, recognizes by that name with its Tama Reservation. Kansas: six pieces. The Kickapoo Reservation (1770) and the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Nation Reservation (2980, whose code was entered before for the nation's trust land in Illinois) lie wholly in Kansas; 69.4%% of the Iowa (KS-NE) Reservation (1590) and all of its trust land, and 33.1%% of the Sac and Fox Nation Reservation (3285) and 70.3%% of its trust land, are in Kansas, entered with Kansas only, since Nebraska is not yet covered. Oregon: 18 pieces under 11 codes. Celilo Village (0560), a trust land whose Census name names no nation, is entered under `governments` with the Confederated Tribes of the Warm Springs Reservation of Oregon, the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation and the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation: the Oregon Blue Book (Oregon Secretary of State, sos.oregon.gov/blue-book/government/Pages/national-tribes-intro.aspx, read 2026-11-13) says Celilo Village is jointly administered by the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs, the Confederated Tribes of Umatilla and the Yakama Indian Nation. The Umatilla Reservation (4405) is given its Oregon piece and 28.6%% of its off-reservation trust land, beside the Washington piece entered before, and the Fort McDermitt Indian Reservation (1210) its Oregon piece, 52.0%%, beside Nevada's. Utah: nine pieces. The Navajo Nation Reservation (2430) is given its Utah piece, 8.9%%, and the Goshute Reservation (1340) its Utah piece, 41.6%%; the Ute Mountain Reservation (4470) has 1.3%% of its area in Utah, 30.584 km2, and its off-reservation trust land lies wholly in Utah; the Uintah and Ouray Reservation (4390, 17,671.391 km2), the Paiute (UT) Reservation (2625), the Skull Valley Reservation (3840) and the Northwestern Shoshone Reservation (2505) lie wholly in the state.

stateRecognition.law: the Connecticut General Statutes, whose chapter 824 gives the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection the care of its reservation (section 47-65)
stateRecognition.publisher: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
stateRecognition.nameFrom: the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection's tribal affairs page
stateRecognition.why: The United States does not recognize this tribe, so the Bureau of Indian Affairs lists no government for this land. The tribal affairs page of Connecticut's Department of Energy and Environmental Protection, which manages the state's reservations under section 47-65 of the Connecticut General Statutes, names it a state recognized tribe and says it keeps two reservations, a quarter of an acre in Trumbull and 106 acres in Colchester. The page gives no office town, so the card gives none. Drawn as New York's and Virginia's state reservations are, on Adam's ruling of 2026-10-10 and the Virginia plan he accepted on 2026-10-22.

stateRecognition.law: Joint Resolution 54 of the General Assembly, 25 March 1983
stateRecognition.publisher: Secretary of the Commonwealth of Virginia
stateRecognition.nameFrom: the Secretary of the Commonwealth's list of state-recognized tribes
stateRecognition.why: The United States does not recognize this tribe, so the Bureau of Indian Affairs lists no government for this land. The Secretary of the Commonwealth's page on the tribe says Joint Resolution 54 recognized it on 25 March 1983 and that it is governed by a chief, an assistant chief and seven council members; the Secretary's list of state-recognized tribes gives its office in West Point and its website. Drawn on the Virginia plan's recommendation, which Adam accepted on 2026-10-22, as New York's state reservations are drawn on his ruling of 2026-10-10.

stateRecognition.law: the law that created the Alabama Indian Affairs Commission (Code of Alabama, section 41-9-708)
stateRecognition.nameFrom: the Alabama Indian Affairs Commission's list of tribes recognized by the State of Alabama
stateRecognition.why: The United States does not recognize this band, so the Bureau of Indian Affairs lists no government for this land. The Alabama Indian Affairs Commission's list of tribes recognized by the State of Alabama (revised 10 June 2026) names it and gives its office in Mount Vernon; the Commission's rules (Alabama Administrative Code chapter 475-X-1, made under section 41-9-708) seat a member for each of the nine tribes, the MOWA Band among them, and the Commission's list of state-recognized tribes says the Commission was created by statute in 1984. Only the town is carried, never the street. Drawn as New York's and Virginia's state reservations are, on Adam's ruling of 2026-10-10 and the Virginia plan he accepted on 2026-10-22.

stateRecognition.law: Code Section 44-12-300 of the Official Code of Georgia, as amended by House Bill 43 of 2024
stateRecognition.publisher: Office of the Governor of Georgia
stateRecognition.why: The United States does not recognize this tribe, so the Bureau of Indian Affairs lists no government for this land. House Bill 43, which the Governor signed in 2024, amends Code Section 44-12-300 to read that the State of Georgia officially recognizes the Lower Muscogee Creek Tribe, Tama Reservation, Whigham, Georgia, as a legitimate American Indian tribe of Georgia. Only the town is carried, never the street. Drawn as New York's and Virginia's state reservations are, on Adam's ruling of 2026-10-10 and the Virginia plan he accepted on 2026-10-22.
